articles.title: The forenses transporter who saved a life: The moment a technician saw a 'dead' baby moving under the morgue sheet
articles.standfirst: Vincent, 18 months old, was declared dead after suffering a suspected drowning in Arizona
articles.summary: Vincent, 18 months old, was declared dead after suffering a suspected drowning in Arizona
articles.body:
Alexus Fiordilino will never forget the moment when she hugged her 18-month-old son, Vincent, to say goodbye to him and thought she heard that he was still breathing. The doctor treating him assured her that these were his final gasps and confirmed his death . However, five hours later, the family received a call that changed everything: the little boy was alive and had been found breathing in the morgue of a hospital in Arizona.

The incident occurred almost nine months ago at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, in the town of Gilbert, and has caused renewed shock after new details about what happened came to light. In an interview with NBC News , Fiordilino, 30, acknowledged that she still regrets not trusting her instinct when she thought she sensed that her son was still alive . " As a mother, you don’t want to hear that. I didn’t want him to suffer. It seemed like they had done everything possible ," she explained, recalling the words of Dr. Aryan Toosi, who allegedly told her that trying new maneuvers to save the little boy would only prolong his agony.

Vincent suffered an alleged drowning and was treated at the hospital. However, he was pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m. on Super Bowl Sunday. Nevertheless, several testimonies collected in police reports indicate that the child may have continued showing signs of breathing after his death had been certified.

'The officers heard "gasping" after his death'

The case has raised doubts about the actions of the healthcare staff. According to police reports, the officers who were in the emergency department observed that the little boy seemed to still be having difficulty breathing after having been declared dead. One of the police officers said he had heard " an audible gasp ." When he returned approximately an hour later to photograph the body, he stated that he again observed what appeared to be " a gasp or a release of air ."

The nurse, for her part, maintained that it was agonal breathing and explained that it could be related to the compressions, the oxygen, and the possible pressure exerted by the family members as they said goodbye to the child. However, when the medical examiner's team arrived hours later to collect the body, they realized that Vincent was still breathing. By then, around five hours had passed since his death had been certified.

The family then received the news that the little boy was still alive, although he needed hospital care and medical assistance. " My husband and I screamed with relief. We were praising the Lord. We were crying. Going from hearing that he was gone to finding out that he is not gone is an indescribable feeling ," Fiordilino recalled.

The family is preparing a complaint against the doctor and the hospital

Medical conduct is now at the center of the controversy. The mother's lawyer, John Brewer, has announced that he plans to file a formal complaint against Dr. Toosi and the hospital over what happened. " The parents were forced to decide whether they should keep trying to resuscitate their son and the doctor provided them with false information ," stressed the attorney, who believes that what happened constitutes a serious lack of respect for human life.

For his part, the doctor's defense has expressed regret over the situation and wished the child a speedy recovery. " Dr. Toosi extends his sympathies to the young patient and his family, and wishes the child a speedy recovery ," it said in a statement in which he also reaffirmed his commitment to quality medical care. As for the hospital, it described what happened as " heartbreaking ," although it declined to offer details about the care provided to the minor for privacy reasons. " Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities ," it said in a statement. The Prosecutor's Office had not yet made a decision on reviewing the case at the time this information was released.

The little boy suffers a severe brain injury and is recovering at home

The little boy's story has also been surrounded by controversy from the beginning. After the alleged drowning, Gilbert Police recommended filing child abuse charges against the parents, after both admitted they had lost sight of Vincent during a party held for the Super Bowl. According to the police report, they also admitted to having smoked marijuana that morning. Ultimately, Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell announced that no charges would be filed against Alexus Fiordilino and her husband.

Now, the family's main concern is the boy's health. Vincent suffers from a severe brain injury, cannot swallow, has seizures, and cannot sit up or crawl on his own, according to the information released about his condition. Despite the aftereffects, the little boy has been able to return home, where he continues recovering with his parents. His case has reopened the debate over the circumstances of his declaration of death and the possible responsibilities arising from what happened at the hospital.

Vincent suffered an alleged drowning and was treated at the hospital. However, he was pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m. on Super Bowl Sunday. Nevertheless, several testimonies collected in police reports indicate that the child may have continued showing signs of breathing after his death had been certified.
'The officers heard "gasping" after his death'

The case has raised doubts about the actions of the healthcare staff. According to police reports, the officers who were in the emergency department observed that the little boy seemed to still be having difficulty breathing after having been declared dead. One of the police officers said he had heard " an audible gasp ." When he returned approximately an hour later to photograph the body, he stated that he again observed what appeared to be " a gasp or a release of air ."

The nurse, for her part, maintained that it was agonal breathing and explained that it could be related to the compressions, the oxygen, and the possible pressure exerted by the family members as they said goodbye to the child. However, when the medical examiner's team arrived hours later to collect the body, they realized that Vincent was still breathing. By then, around five hours had passed since his death had been certified.

The family then received the news that the little boy was still alive, although he needed hospital care and medical assistance. " My husband and I screamed with relief. We were praising the Lord. We were crying. Going from hearing that he was gone to finding out that he is not gone is an indescribable feeling ," Fiordilino recalled.
The family is preparing a complaint against the doctor and the hospital

Medical conduct is now at the center of the controversy. The mother's lawyer, John Brewer, has announced that he plans to file a formal complaint against Dr. Toosi and the hospital over what happened. " The parents were forced to decide whether they should keep trying to resuscitate their son and the doctor provided them with false information ," stressed the attorney, who believes that what happened constitutes a serious lack of respect for human life.

For his part, the doctor's defense has expressed regret over the situation and wished the child a speedy recovery. " Dr. Toosi extends his sympathies to the young patient and his family, and wishes the child a speedy recovery ," it said in a statement in which he also reaffirmed his commitment to quality medical care. As for the hospital, it described what happened as " heartbreaking ," although it declined to offer details about the care provided to the minor for privacy reasons. " Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities ," it said in a statement. The Prosecutor's Office had not yet made a decision on reviewing the case at the time this information was released.
The little boy suffers a severe brain injury and is recovering at home

The little boy's story has also been surrounded by controversy from the beginning. After the alleged drowning, Gilbert Police recommended filing child abuse charges against the parents, after both admitted they had lost sight of Vincent during a party held for the Super Bowl. According to the police report, they also admitted to having smoked marijuana that morning. Ultimately, Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell announced that no charges would be filed against Alexus Fiordilino and her husband.

Now, the family's main concern is the boy's health. Vincent suffers from a severe brain injury, cannot swallow, has seizures, and cannot sit up or crawl on his own, according to the information released about his condition. Despite the aftereffects, the little boy has been able to return home, where he continues recovering with his parents. His case has reopened the debate over the circumstances of his declaration of death and the possible responsibilities arising from what happened at the hospital.

articles.title: How Social Security benefits are calculated based on your lifetime earnings? This is how you can calculate them
articles.standfirst: The government uses decades of earnings to calculate benefits, and missing employment years may affect your monthly payment
articles.summary: The government uses decades of earnings to calculate benefits, and missing employment years may affect your monthly payment
articles.body:
A higher salary late in your career does not necessarily guarantee a significantly larger Social Security check. The amount you receive in retirement reflects decades of earnings, meaning decisions made long before leaving the workforce can affect your financial future.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) calculates retirement benefits using an individual's earnings history rather than simply considering their most recent salary or the total amount contributed through payroll taxes.

The system also rewards people who delay claiming benefits beyond their full retirement age, while reducing monthly payments for those who begin collecting earlier.

Understanding these calculations can help workers identify opportunities to increase their retirement income and avoid overlooking mistakes in their official earnings records.

Your 35 highest-earning years determine benefits

The calculation begins with the SSA reviewing earnings from employment covered by Social Security taxes throughout a worker's career.

Historical earnings are adjusted to account for changes in average national wages, allowing income earned decades ago to be compared with more recent salaries.

The agency then selects the worker's 35 highest-earning years and divides the combined adjusted earnings by 420 months.

This produces a figure known as Average Indexed Monthly Earnings , or AIME, which forms the foundation of the retirement benefit calculation.

However, employment gaps can make a substantial difference. Workers with fewer than 35 years of qualifying earnings have zero-income years included in their average.

Someone who worked for only 30 years, for example, would have five years counted as zero, potentially lowering their eventual monthly payment.

Lifetime earnings turned into monthly payments

After calculating AIME, the SSA applies a progressive formula to determine the Primary Insurance Amount , which is generally the benefit payable at full retirement age.

For workers first eligible in 2026, the calculation uses three earnings brackets:

90 percent of the first $1,286 in average indexed monthly earnings.

32 percent of earnings between $1,286 and $7,749.

15 percent of earnings above $7,749.

These thresholds, known as bend points, are adjusted annually to reflect changes in national wages.

The formula provides proportionally greater benefits to lower-income workers, although those with higher lifetime earnings generally receive larger monthly payments.

Claiming Social Security at 62 could mean smaller check

Even after the basic benefit is established, the age at which someone begins collecting Social Security can significantly influence their payment.

Americans can claim retirement benefits as early as age 62, but those born in 1960 or later face a 30 percent reduction if they claim five years before their full retirement age of 67.

Waiting until age 70 can instead increase monthly benefits to approximately 124 percent of the full retirement amount.

Continuing to work may also raise future payments when additional earnings replace lower-income years in the original calculation.

How to check your estimated Social Security benefits

Workers can review their earnings history and projected retirement payments through their personal my Social Security account.

The online service provides estimates based on recorded earnings and allows users to compare potential benefits at different claiming ages.

Annual cost-of-living adjustments can increase payments after retirement, while errors in employment records should be corrected promptly.

The important distinction is that Social Security benefits aren't determined by one particularly successful year. They reflect a lifetime of earnings, with the timing of retirement providing another opportunity to influence the final amount.

articles.title: Defying the 22nd Amendment: Trump Claims He Has a 'Right' to Run in 2028 Because 'They Cheated Me' in 2020
articles.standfirst: 'He has addressed the Constitutional Amendment that limits presidents to two terms: "I think the law says that I am not allowed to run again. I have studied that phrase..."'
articles.summary: 'He has addressed the Constitutional Amendment that limits presidents to two terms: "I think the law says that I am not allowed to run again. I have studied that phrase..."'
articles.body:
The President Donald Trump never ceases to surprise with his style of interpreting issues such as the one he has now brought up. Namely, whether he can run again in an election. During a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of the upcoming legislative elections, the leader suggested that he has the "right" to run for the presidency again in 2028 , arguing that the 2020 election was "stolen" from him and "rigged."

And it was then that he brought out all his heavy artillery by citing an example from the past. Trump addressed the Amendment to the U.S. Constitution that limits presidential terms to two . "I think the law says I'm not allowed to run again. I've studied that phrase ... Unfortunately , it's quite concise and there isn't much room for maneuver," the president initially acknowledged .

'But then, he has justified a possible candidacy by referring to his defeat against Joe Biden in 2020 : "They cheated us in the second one because we won three times. So I think I have the right to run again. I think I have the right to run again because they cheated. They rigged the election" .'

Contentious elections in the US in 2020

" State authorities and his own Department of Justice confirmed the election was clean and dismissed the allegations for lack of evidence, but Trump has always maintained that the results had been taken away from him.

The tension caused by that conflict rose even further when on January 6, 2021, the storming of the Capitol by a mob of his supporters took place, who violently broke into the seat of Congress in an attempt to stop the certification of Biden's victory.

articles.title: Sitting Bull, Legendary Native American Leader: “Let us put our minds together and see what life we can make for our children”
articles.standfirst: Sitting Bull was a pivotal figure in the Indians' resistance against the United States government in the 1800s.
articles.summary: Sitting Bull was a pivotal figure in the Indians' resistance against the United States government in the 1800s.
articles.body:
If you do a Google search of the most famous Native Americans in history, Sitting Bull is the name at the top of the list. Sitting Bull was a spiritual leader and chief for the Hunkpapa Lakota tribe, and became renowned for his efforts of resistance against the United States government and its new policies in the 1800s.

Sitting Bull was born sometime around 1831 . It's unclear exactly where he was born. Many believe it was along the Grand River in South Dakota , though his great-grandson once suggested he was born along the Yellowstone River in Montana . The first name given to him was actually " Jumping Badger ", and his nickname was " Slow " due to his careful nature. He was later named " Buffalo Bull Who Sits Down " by his father at 14 years old, but Americans commonly refer to him as Sitting Bull .

As he grew older, Sitting Bull became involved in conflicts with United States army parties and other tribes . His most famous conflict came in 1876 , dubbed the Battle of the Little Bighorn . The U.S. Army began treating those living off the Great Sioux Reservation , which included Sitting Bull's Lakota tribe. Thus began the Great Sioux War of 1876 .

The Battle of the Little Bighorn took place on June 25-26, 1876 in Montana. Sitting Bull had a vision of a Native American victory over the United States and their allied Crows and Arikaras tribes . Sitting Bull's vision came true, as the Lakota , Dakota , Northern Cheyenne , and Arapaho tribes handed their opponents a major defeat.

Sitting Bull was ultimately pressured out of the United States not long after, though. After being chased out due to not surrendering, as American military forces continued to cover more ground, Sitting Bull and his band went North to Canada . He remained in exile for four years, before returning to the United States in 1881 and surrendering .

He settled in the Standing Rock Reservation , then joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West show in the mid-1880s. In his mid-50s, U.S. agent James McLaughlin ordered Sitting Bull's arrest, out of fear he was soon to flee the reservation. A standoff took place on December 15, which resulted in bloodshed and the death of Sitting Bull via gunshot by Indian agency police at his home .

While many inspiring quotes from Sitting Bull continue to fortify his legacy, one stands out over the rest, due to his vision of the future: " Let us put our minds together and see what life we can make for our children ."

articles.title: Terrifying moment huge waves slam into a moving Amtrak train in California
articles.standfirst: The force of the ocean is raising new questions about the effects of an extreme climate phenomenon.
articles.summary: The force of the ocean is raising new questions about the effects of an extreme climate phenomenon.
articles.body:
This week, several videos captured one of the most striking scenes along the California coast: enormous waves slammed into an Amtrak passenger train as it traveled alongside the Pacific Ocean, covering its cars in sea foam. The footage quickly raised questions about what caused the powerful surf and how it relates to a Super Niño .

What does the Super Niño have to do with the huge waves?

Super Niño could play a role in what is happening across the Pacific. The phenomenon is characterized by unusually intense warming of surface waters , which can alter weather patterns and change storm activity in different regions.

When these changes affect ocean conditions, waves can grow stronger and reach exposed stretches of coastline. In San Clemente, California, the railroad tracks run alongside the shore, allowing waves to reach the rail infrastructure directly.

Why does the surf pose a risk to the tracks?

The danger does not end when the water recedes. Powerful waves can erode the ground and wash away the materials supporting the tracks , compromising the stability of the rail line and potentially disrupting train service.

With Super Niño conditions still a concern, changes in the Pacific will be key to understanding what could happen along the California coast in the coming months , particularly in areas where powerful surf threatens infrastructure built along the shoreline.

Eleven of the victims sustained gunshot wounds, and at least three victims sustained serious injuries, according to police.

The university said on social media that the shooting happened near its campus and that it remained safe.

articles.title: Breaking Katie Zacharia’s record: Britt McHenry’s 24-hour rise and fall at the Trump-era State Department
articles.standfirst: A same-day promotion turned into a swift departure after McHenry’s confrontation with spectators at a Washington Wizards game
articles.summary: A same-day promotion turned into a swift departure after McHenry’s confrontation with spectators at a Washington Wizards game
articles.body:
Britt McHenry’s latest career controversy has thrust the former ESPN reporter into the headlines again, this time following her brief stint in the Trump administration.

McHenry resigned from her position as a US State Department press adviser after a confrontation with spectators at an NBA game in Washington, DC, reportedly ending her government career just one day after receiving a promotion.

The incident occurred Wednesday night at Capital One Arena during a Washington Wizards game against the Milwaukee Bucks.

According to reports published by ABC News and Page Six, McHenry’s resignation followed footage showing her throwing a drink toward people in the stands before being escorted from the venue. The timing was particularly striking because she’d reportedly secured a significant career advancement earlier that same day.

A promotion overshadowed by a public confrontation

McHenry , 40, had joined the State Department the previous month as a press adviser covering Europe and Africa. Page Six reported that she was later promoted to lead External Affairs and Press for Under Secretary Jacob Helberg’s team.

However, the opportunity was short-lived, with a source telling the publication that she was forced to resign following the arena confrontation.

The dispute reportedly began when spectators made insulting comments about Milwaukee Bucks player Kyle Kuzma and his fiancée, model Winnie Harlow.

According to a source cited by Page Six, McHenry intervened and urged the hecklers to ease up. The situation subsequently escalated, with competing accounts emerging about what happened next.

A source claimed that spectators threw a drink at McHenry . However, video obtained by TMZ appears to show her throwing a drink toward people in the crowd as spectators chant for her to leave. She was then escorted from the stands, leaving amid boos and reportedly blowing kisses toward the crowd.

Although the footage captures part of the confrontation, it doesn't establish every detail of how the dispute began. A State Department spokesperson declined to comment on McHenry’s departure, describing it as an internal personnel matter.

The controversy has revived memories of McHenry’s previous professional setback, which also involved footage of her behavior becoming widely circulated online.

In 2015, ESPN suspended McHenry for one week after a video showed her berating an employee at a Washington towing company. Following her car’s removal, she launched into a series of personal insults, questioning the worker’s education, abilities and employment circumstances.

The clip attracted widespread criticism and became a defining controversy during her broadcasting career.

Her latest departure has drawn renewed attention to that earlier episode, creating uncomfortable parallels between her experiences in television and government communications. Both incidents involved public confrontations captured on video, although the circumstances surrounding each were different.

McHenry’s brief government tenure has therefore ended under a cloud of controversy, with her reported promotion quickly eclipsed by the arena incident. Rather than marking a new chapter in her career, the appointment has become notable for how abruptly it ended.

articles.title: Who is Pete Hegseth, the United States Secretary of Defense who has expelled trans people from the military
articles.standfirst: Some Navy and Marine Corps commanders have disobeyed the order and are looking for ways to keep the affected people in the ranks
articles.summary: Some Navy and Marine Corps commanders have disobeyed the order and are looking for ways to keep the affected people in the ranks
articles.body:
Pete Hegseth , an Army National Guard veteran with Bronze Star decorations for his deployments in Iraq and Afghanistan , first came to public attention mainly as a host on Fox News , a media outlet aligned with Donald Trump , before being appointed Secretary of Defense by the current President.

Known for his alignment with the hardline conservative wing and his critical stance against progressive policies within the Armed Forces , the head of the Pentagon restructured military policy under the premise that service should be reserved for those who meet traditional standards of physical and mental fitness . During a mass event before sailors and Marines, the secretary of Defense used a derogatory term to announce that he would expel transgender soldiers , pushing a strict bureaucratic review process to carry out their removal.

The Navy and the United States Marine Corps, against Pete Hegseth's decision

The directive designed by the Pentagon seemed inflexible: a mechanism whereby separation boards were required to process discharges without hesitation . To carry out the measure, extremely rigid instructions were issued under which board members were told to "circle certain words" that would certify a trans status in order to proceed with automatic dismissal. However, just a few steps from the auditorium where Hegseth spoke, at Quantico Base, the boards tasked with enforcing those orders were doing the opposite . What the Government had envisioned as a meteoric purge has run headlong into the troops' own judgment.

The ban argues that transgender people represent a costly burden on military effectiveness . However, the practical implementation in the Navy and the Marine Corps has taken an unexpected turn. Instead of meekly complying with the expulsion directives, the boards rebelled and voted in favor of allowing them to stay , prioritizing their colleagues' professional performance over ideological mandates. This phenomenon of veiled insubordination stands in sharp contrast to the pattern seen in the Army or the Air Force, where most hearings have resulted in immediate dismissals.

'The contradiction between the Pentagon's rhetoric and the reality of the military courts has become evident. While high-ranking officials point to diversity as an operational obstacle, in the Marines' hearings passionate defenses of group cohesion have emerged. In the case of Sergeant Damien Contreras , the review board decided to strike the clause on a history of hormone therapy from his findings sheet and include the phrase "remains qualified" in order to keep him on active duty, valuing his decade of impeccable service above the restrictions imposed by the administration.'

Legal experts and former military lawyers point out that this institutional brake reflects a deep sense of camaraderie. Former Air Force lawyer Rachel VanLandingham praised the judges' stance in The New York Times, noting that the boards are saying "they are not going to play that game" , refusing to endorse incoherent records or proceedings they consider outright unfair. This quiet resistance exposes a growing gap between the directives issued by the top brass and the values of loyalty on the front lines.

When the fulfillment of duty is above any directive: this is the devastating message

Although the number of favorable rulings is small and they could be overturned by politically appointed secretaries, the message sent by the Navy and the Marine Corps is devastating . In the Navy, where the percentage of diverse personnel is estimated to be higher than in other branches, career officers have argued that their subordinates have always carried out their duty impeccably. The troops are choosing to protect the effectiveness of their units rather than submit to arbitrary impositions.

The attempt to homogenize the armed forces through sweeping dismissals thus encounters an unexpected obstacle: the very judgment of military personnel who prioritize merit in the fulfillment of duty . In the Marine Corps, whose motto is Semper Fidelis, the respect earned after years of service and deployments carries more weight than the directives of a purge imposed from Pentagon offices.

articles.title: Nicki Minaj joins Trump at a rally on Air Force One and he praises her "beautiful ass": "It's hard not to notice it"
articles.standfirst: The artist has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement and supports the president in every way she can
articles.summary: The artist has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement and supports the president in every way she can
articles.body:
The relationship between Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump shows clear signs of great cordiality and affinity . The Trinidadian rapper accompanied the President of the United States aboard Air Force One this weekend on the way to a campaign event held in Michigan to support the Republican Senate candidate, Mike Rogers . Over the years, the artist has become one of his most visible supporters. Her support for the president has been reflected in various public appearances alongside members of the Republican Administration.

The latest sign of that closeness came through a video shared on X by Steven Cheung, White House communications director. In the footage, Minaj appears inside the presidential plane praising the policies promoted by Trump. " I think we've found the new White House press secretary," Cheung joked in the post. The singer responded to the comment with a laughing emoji.

Although Minaj did not speak at the rally, she did show her support with her presence, and it was Trump himself who wanted to make an aside about it. The president then made a striking remark by praising her "beautiful butt." "Stand up, it's hard not to see it," the president told the crowd.

Minaj has declared herself Trump's "number one fan"

The event had as its main objective to boost Mike Rogers's candidacy , who is facing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in a closely contested race for a Senate seat. The upcoming midterm elections on November 3 will be key in determining control of the U.S. Congress.

In recent years, Minaj has strengthened her ties with the American conservative movement . The singer, who has millions of followers grouped under the name Barbz, has even gone so far as to declare herself Trump's "number one fan."

Minaj's brutal contrast with Trump over these years

The rapprochement is striking considering that in 2018 she harshly criticized the Republican's immigration policy and revealed that she had arrived in the United States irregularly when she was just five years old . Already in January of this year, she claimed to have received for free a "gold card" promoted by Trump , a controversial program linked to obtaining permanent residency for foreigners who make significant economic contributions to the U.S. government.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday, October 26 drawing for the $687 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $687 million for Monday night's drawing
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $687 million for Monday night's drawing
articles.body:
Lottery players across the United States are preparing for another chance to win a life-changing prize as Powerball returns on Monday, October 26, with an estimated jackpot of $687 million.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, and the top prize has continued to grow after nobody matched all six numbers in Saturday's draw.

According to the official Powerball website, the jackpot's estimated cash value is $294.7 million before applicable taxes.

Monday's winning numbers have not yet been confirmed. The drawing will take place later tonight, meaning players should consult the official Powerball website once the results are published rather than rely on numbers from previous draws.

The growing prize offers another opportunity for ticket holders to dream of becoming multimillionaires. However, winning the jackpot requires matching all five white-ball numbers and the separate red Powerball number, making the odds extremely challenging.

What were the latest Powerball winning numbers?

The most recent completed drawing took place on Saturday, October 24, 2026. The winning numbers were 4, 5, 15, 19 and 55, with 19 as the Powerball .

The Power Play multiplier was 2X. No ticket matched all six numbers to claim the jackpot, allowing the estimated prize to increase to $687 million for Monday's draw.

Players waiting for Monday's results can check the official Powerball website after the drawing. The site publishes the winning combination, prize information and details about tickets that matched the required numbers.

Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET. Tickets cost $2 per play, although players can add the Power Play feature for an additional $1. This option can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes, but it does not increase the jackpot itself.

The jackpot winner can choose between an annuity paid through 30 graduated payments over 29 years or a lump-sum cash payment.

The advertised jackpot and cash value are estimates before federal and applicable local taxes, so the amount a winner ultimately receives may be considerably lower.

How difficult is it to win the $687 million jackpot?

Powerball's jackpot odds are approximately 1 in 292.2 million, according to lottery information published by participating state lotteries. The overall odds of winning any prize are around 1 in 24.9.

Players must select five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. They can choose their own combination or ask a lottery terminal to generate a random selection.

Matching fewer numbers can still produce a prize, with payouts depending on the combination matched and whether the ticket includes Power Play. The jackpot, however, requires all six numbers to be correct.

For anyone holding a ticket for Monday's drawing, the important step is to wait for the official results and check the numbers carefully.

Because the October 26 drawing has yet to take place, the winning combination and whether anyone claims the $687 million prize remain unknown.

The next scheduled drawing after Monday is Wednesday, October 28, at 10:59 p.m. ET. If nobody wins the jackpot on Monday, the prize is expected to roll over and grow again, although the next advertised amount will depend on ticket sales and official lottery estimates.

articles.title: Viral: He ordered a $30 filet mignon at Texas Roadhouse and claims they served him a cheaper cut for the third time
articles.standfirst: Kenneth Card reported on TikTok that he received a sirloin instead of the filet he had ordered at a restaurant. The chain confirmed an error on one of his visits, although it said it could not verify that it had happened on three occasions.
articles.summary: Kenneth Card reported on TikTok that he received a sirloin instead of the filet he had ordered at a restaurant. The chain confirmed an error on one of his visits, although it said it could not verify that it had happened on three occasions.
articles.body:
Kenneth Card, a regular Texas Roadhouse customer, claims he received a cheaper cut of meat than the one he ordered on three different visits to the restaurant. His complaint began circulating on TikTok and has already surpassed 30,000 views.

Card had ordered an eight-ounce filet mignon, which costs around $30 at that establishment, but he claims that a much lower-priced and lower-quality product appeared on his plate.

His experience in kitchens made him notice the difference

The man explained that he worked for years in hotel and restaurant kitchens, where he prepared and cut meat, so he was used to distinguishing the different cuts. "I know what type of meat I'm getting when it's served to me", he explained as he recounted how he detected the alleged switch.

Card said he has visited that Texas Roadhouse about once a week for more than a year and had even developed a close relationship with some employees. According to his account, the first time he received the wrong cut he informed the staff and they replaced the dish with a filet . On another visit, he decided to eat the meat without complaining.

The third occasion was different. The customer decided to speak with a manager and said that the restaurant took the plate back to verify what type of meat they had served him. According to Card, the employees ended up acknowledging that it was not the cut he had ordered and prepared a new one, which he decided to take home.

"This is the third time they've tried to sell me a sirloin, or any other type of meat that isn't a filet", Card recalled about his conversation with the staff. He later posted the video because, as he explained, he wanted to warn other customers to make sure they were getting what they had paid for.

The difference between the two cuts was also one of the points that sparked debate among those who watched the video. Card described the filet as a much more tender meat , while the sirloin has a firmer texture and requires more chewing. Some users acknowledged in the comments that they probably would not know how to tell them apart if something similar happened to them.

Texas Roadhouse responded to the allegations and confirmed that it was able to verify at least one error in the order. A spokesperson explained that the company "has not been able to confirm that this happened on three occasions," but noted that, in the confirmed incident, management quickly corrected the problem and gave the customer the filet he had requested .

The chain added that its employees check dishes before they leave the kitchen to verify the quality and accuracy of each order, and recommended that customers immediately alert the waiter if they believe they have received the wrong cut. Card, for his part, said that after what happened he does not plan to return to the Forsyth restaurant: "I think I'm done going there. I'll try somewhere else."

articles.title: El Niño bringing a brutal winter to the U.S. and how should Americans prepare?
articles.standfirst: El Niño could intensify storms across several regions of the United States during the winter of 2026-2027.
articles.summary: El Niño could intensify storms across several regions of the United States during the winter of 2026-2027.
articles.body:
Fall is underway across the United States, and although the official start of winter is still several weeks away , the weather is already becoming a factor in plans for the coming months. Between holiday travel, family gatherings, and Christmas preparations, there is one thing worth taking care of early: getting ready for weather conditions that could complicate the winter season.

One factor meteorologists are watching for the winter of 2026-2027 is El Niño, a climate phenomenon that can alter rainfall patterns , storm tracks, and temperatures across different regions. Its effects will not be the same everywhere in the country, but some scenarios point to a season with significant rainfall.

Which regions of the U.S. could face the most challenges?

Florida and parts of the East Coast could experience periods of frequent rainfall, severe storms, and flooding . California and other parts of the Southwest could also see significant precipitation, although its distribution and intensity will depend on how weather conditions develop.

In the Northeast, milder temperatures would not rule out coastal storms, while some areas of the Midwest could see less snowfall early in the season.

How to prepare your home before winter arrives

Waiting until a storm is approaching to inspect your home can leave little time to react. Fall is a good opportunity to check the condition of your roof and windows, as well as areas where leaks could develop . Cleaning gutters, clearing drains, and making sure your heating system is working properly can also help prevent problems when temperatures drop or rainfall increases.

If you live in a flood-prone area, identify routes to safer locations and stay informed about alerts from local authorities. It is also important to secure outdoor furniture and other items that could be blown around by strong winds.

Having an emergency kit ready can also provide peace of mind if a storm causes power outages or makes it impossible to leave home. Keep drinking water, nonperishable food, flashlights, batteries, portable chargers, a first-aid kit, and any medications your family needs . Store copies of important documents in a protected place, and agree on how to stay in touch with loved ones if regular communication services become unavailable.

How to protect your Christmas plans from bad weather

The holiday season often brings road trips, family visits, and days away from home. However, a sudden change in weather conditions can disrupt any itinerary. Before traveling, check the forecast for your entire route, review official weather alerts, and check road conditions . If storms are expected, consider changing your departure time or finding a safer alternative.

If you plan to spend several days away, make sure your home is prepared for the expected temperatures and ask someone you trust to check on it if a problem arises.

articles.title: Trump has it in for Norway, which he calls a "shithole country": the reason, not awarding him the Nobel Peace Prize
articles.standfirst: The President has a chip on his shoulder about it and whenever he can, he takes aim at the Scandinavian country and the award organizers
articles.summary: The President has a chip on his shoulder about it and whenever he can, he takes aim at the Scandinavian country and the award organizers
articles.body:
The President Donald Trump , has it in for Norway . Very much so, judging by how he has been expressing himself. And the latest incident, in the final stretch of the campaign for the midterm elections next Tuesday, November 3, did nothing but cross the line. He called Norway a “shithole country” for not having received the Nobel Peace Prize , in addition to reviving his insults against Libya, Yemen, Haiti, and Somalia.

The U.S. president has linked his refusal to accept Norwegian immigrants to the Norwegian Nobel Committee’s decision not to award him the 2026 prize.

The US president has declared to his supporters: “I don’t want anyone from Norway. I don’t want to have anything to do with Norway” . And he has argued that he has resolved eight wars and has two more on the way, referring to his supposed diplomatic efforts.

Previously, Trump had already lashed out harshly on another occasion. At the beginning of October, he called it a “stain Norway will never wash away” that they did not award him the prize. And he is sticking to his guns... He continues his campaign to discredit the Nordic country.

In the face of such statements, the Nordic country's foreign minister had to step in yesterday and tell public broadcaster NRK that Trump knows that the committee is independent. “We have reminded him of that, in case anyone was wondering, and that remains the case” , he said on the matter. The Norwegian government has declined to comment further despite the lack of respect shown by Trump once again following the awarding of the latest Nobel Peace Prize.

articles.summary: The next GI Bill payment window is approaching, with enrollment verification and banking schedules determining when money arrives
articles.body:
V eterans and students relying on GI Bill benefits to cover housing and education expenses should expect their next monthly payment in early November, although the exact date money reaches their bank accounts may vary.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) normally processes Post-9/11 GI Bill monthly benefits on the first day of each month, with electronic payments potentially taking up to five business days to arrive.

In November 2026, the scheduled processing date falls on Sunday, November 1, meaning recipients should allow additional time for banks to handle their deposits.

Under the VA's standard payment guidance, eligible students can generally expect funds during the first week of November, although individual processing circumstances may affect the actual arrival date.

The payment arriving in November covers eligible enrollment during October. Benefits earned through attendance in November are normally paid at the beginning of December.

When will November 2026 VA education benefits be deposited?

The VA's regular processing schedule points to November 1 as the date payments are initiated, rather than a guaranteed date when recipients will see funds in their accounts.

Because November 1 falls on a weekend, Monday, November 2, through Friday, November 6, represents the expected five-business-day arrival window for standard electronic payments.

However, that period is an estimate, and deposits may arrive later depending on individual circumstances.

First-time beneficiaries may experience different processing times. The VA advises that initial direct deposits generally arrive seven to 10 business days after enrollment verification.

Recipients approved to receive paper checks should allow approximately 14 days after verification for delivery.

Students receiving Post-9/11 GI Bill housing benefits must verify their enrollment each month to continue receiving payments.

The VA requires confirmation that students remained enrolled in their approved courses, helping prevent incorrect payments and potential debts.

Verification can be completed through the VA's online system or other approved methods, including text messages.

Not every student receives the same monthly amount, even when they qualify under the same education benefits program.

Students whose expected deposit hasn't arrived should check their VA payment history, confirm their bank details and ensure their enrollment information is accurate.

articles.standfirst: Payments are due to arrive on Wednesday, October 28
articles.summary: Payments are due to arrive on Wednesday, October 28
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits have scheduled payment dates throughout October 2026, with eligibility for each deposit depending on when benefits began or the recipient's birthdate. Some beneficiaries are due their money on Wednesday, October 28 whilst Social Security retirement, disability and survivor benefits follow a staggered payment schedule for most people who began receiving payments after May 1997.

The Social Security Administration assigns payment dates according to birthdates, while certain long-term recipients follow a separate calendar. Beneficiaries who started receiving Social Security before May 1997 are scheduled to receive their October payment on Friday, October 2. Most other recipients are assigned one of three Wednesdays, depending on their date of birth as the October schedule places recipients born between the first and 10th of any month on Wednesday, October 14. Those born between the 11th and 20th are scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, while people born between the 21st and 31st should receive payment on Wednesday, October 28. These dates cover eligible retirement, disability and survivor benefit recipients under the standard schedule. If your payment has not arrived on the expected date, the SSA recommends checking with your bank or financial institution before reporting a missing deposit. October also brings important dates for people preparing for 2027. Medicare 's annual Open Enrollment Period runs from October 15 through December 7, 2026, allowing beneficiaries to review coverage and make eligible changes for the following year. The SSA 's official website, ssa.gov, provides payment information and program updates. Beneficiaries can also compare Medicare coverage through Medicare.gov before selecting plans for 2027.

When will disability beneficiaries receive their money?

People receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) generally follow the same birthdate-based schedule as retirement and survivor beneficiaries. Therefore, the payment date for October depends on the recipient's birthday, unless a different scheduling rule applies to their benefits. Supplemental Security Income (SSI) follows a separate calendar. SSI recipients are scheduled to receive their October payment on Thursday, October 1, because payments are normally issued on the first day of each month unless that date falls on a weekend or federal holiday. SSI supports eligible older adults and people with disabilities who have limited income and resources. It is a separate program from Social Security Disability Insurance , although some individuals may qualify for both types of assistance. If an electronic payment does not appear on the scheduled date, contact your bank or financial institution first. Processing delays can affect when money becomes visible in an account, even when the SSA has issued the payment. If the money remains missing, late or potentially stolen, contact the SSA at 1-800-772-1213. People who use TTY services can call 1-800-325-0778, or they can contact their local Social Security office for assistance.

articles.title: Who is Hasan Piker? The controversial streamer democrats can’t ignore before Election Day
articles.standfirst: Hasan Piker has become one of the most influential political voices online.
articles.summary: Hasan Piker has become one of the most influential political voices online.
articles.body:
As Democrats seek to regain control of Congress, an unexpected figure has become one of the biggest points of debate within the party: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker .

While progressive sectors consider him a key tool for connecting with young voters, especially men, some moderate Democrats have questioned his statements and describe them as controversial rhetoric .

Hasan Piker, the political streamer who reached millions of people

Piker, 35 years old and born in New Jersey, has built one of the largest digital political audiences in the United States.

His live streams on Twitch reach around 14 million viewers per month and he has nearly 3 million followers on the platform . He also has 1.9 million followers on Instagram an d YouTube , as well as 1.7 million on X .

His influence within the progressive space has made him an increasingly relevant figure for candidates looking to attract a generation of voters accustomed to digital content.

His comments on international politics generate controversy

Piker’s growth has also been accompanied by criticism over some of his statements on U.S. foreign policy , international conflicts, and organizations labeled as terrorist.

Among his most questioned comments was one occasion in which he stated that the United States “deserved” the September 11 attacks .

In various clips from his streams, Piker made comments about historical figures such as Lenin, Fidel Castro, and Che Guevara , as well as statements related to Hamas and Hezbollah that drew rejection from his critics.

These positions have caused a division between those who consider him a new progressive voice and those who believe his comments cross political lines.

Hasan Piker increases his presence within the progressive movement

Identified as a democratic socialist and with longstanding ties to the Democratic Socialists of America , Piker began to get more actively involved in political campaigns in recent years.

In 2026 he endorsed progressive Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Wisconsin gubernatorial hopeful Francesca Hong .

During a stream with Hong, Piker questioned the candidate about proposals such as a one-year pause on new data centers, limiting the power of large agricultural companies, and creating public supermarkets. Hong responded affirmatively to each point.

New York Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who has also appeared on Piker’s streams, defended her decision to engage with him.

In comments to ABC News , she explained that her goal is part of an effort to reach young voters and build a “winning coalition.”

With millions of followers and growing influence in digital politics, Hasan Piker has become a figure impossible for Democrats to ignore : for some he represents an opportunity to connect with a new generation; for others, a risk that could further divide the party.

articles.title: When are Disability Benefits being paid in November 2026? This is the SSDI Payment Schedule for next month
articles.standfirst: Social Security Disability Insurance recipients will receive their November payments on different dates depending on their birth dates and when they first began collecting benefits
articles.summary: Social Security Disability Insurance recipients will receive their November payments on different dates depending on their birth dates and when they first began collecting benefits
articles.body:
Millions of Americans who rely on Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) to help cover their living expenses will want to check the payment calendar ahead of November 2026.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) distributes benefits on a staggered schedule, meaning the exact date a payment arrives depends on the beneficiary's circumstances.

November brings two notable calendar changes. Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, November 11, which affects the usual payment date for one group of beneficiaries.

Meanwhile, S upplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will receive their November payment in October because the first day of the month falls on a Sunday.

According to the SSA's published 2026 payment calendar, most SSDI recipients receive their money on one of three dates, based on the day of the month they were born.

However, people who have been receiving Social Security for many years, as well as certain beneficiaries who collect both Social Security and SSI, follow a separate schedule.

November 2026 SSDI payment dates: When will your money arrive?

For most people receiving SSDI , the payment date is determined by the birth date of the person whose work record is used to calculate the benefits.

Payments are generally scheduled for the second, third or fourth Wednesday of each month, although calendar adjustments can affect the dates.

Here is the November 2026 schedule for the three main groups:

- Tuesday, November 10: Beneficiaries born between the first and tenth of any month. Their regular payment date would fall on the second Wednesday, November 11, but the date is brought forward because of Veterans Day.

- Wednesday, November 18: Beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th of any month.

- Wednesday, November 25: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st of any month.

These dates apply to most SSDI recipients who began receiving benefits after April 30, 1997, and do not fall under one of the exceptions to the standard Wednesday schedule.

People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 generally receive their payments on the third day of each month. The same schedule normally applies to people receiving both Social Security and SSI, although their SSI payment follows its own calendar.

For November, that Social Security payment is scheduled for Tuesday, November 3. Beneficiaries should check their individual records if they are unsure which payment group applies to them.

Why SSI recipients will be paid in October

Although SSDI and SSI are both administered by the SSA, they are different programs with different eligibility requirements.

SSDI is based on a person's qualifying work history and Social Security contributions, while SSI is a needs-based program for eligible people who are older, blind or disabled and have limited income and resources.

SSI payments are normally issued on the first day of each month. Because November 1, 2026, falls on a Sunday, the SSA's calendar schedules the November SSI payment for Friday, October 30.

That means SSI recipients should not expect a separate SSI deposit during November itself. The October 30 payment is the benefit for November, rather than an additional payment or a bonus. The next regular SSI payment after that is scheduled for Tuesday, December 1.

Understanding this distinction is important for households planning their monthly budgets. An early deposit means the money must cover expenses across the month it is intended for, even though it arrives before that month begins.

Beneficiaries should also remember that the amount they receive is separate from the payment date. The calendar determines when the SSA schedules a deposit, not how much an individual qualifies to receive.

Anyone who does not receive a payment on the expected date should first check their bank account and payment details.

The SSA advises beneficiaries to allow three additional mailing days before contacting the agency if a payment has not arrived. People can also review their information through their official my Social Security account or contact the SSA directly for help with an individual payment issue.

With two dates shifting earlier than usual, checking the November calendar now can help SSDI and SSI recipients plan ahead for housing costs, groceries, medical expenses and other essential bills.

articles.title: Who do you vote for in Midterm Elections? Every race that will be decided next Tuesday
articles.standfirst: The 2026 US midterm elections will determine control of Congress, numerous state governments and key local offices, giving voters an opportunity to influence the country's political direction
articles.summary: The 2026 US midterm elections will determine control of Congress, numerous state governments and key local offices, giving voters an opportunity to influence the country's political direction
articles.body:
Americans will head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3, for the 2026 midterm elections.

Although President Donald Trump will not be on the ballot, the results could significantly affect his ability to advance his agenda during the remainder of his second term.

Voters will choose all 435 members of the House of Representatives, a portion of the Senate , governors in 36 states and numerous state and local officials. Some states will also hold votes on ballot measures covering specific laws or constitutional changes.

Midterm elections take place halfway through a president's four-year term. They often serve as a public assessment of the administration's performance, while determining which party controls Congress and sets its legislative priorities.

Which congressional races will be decided?

Every seat in the House of Representatives is contested, with all members serving two-year terms. The Senate has a different system, with six-year terms staggered so that roughly one-third of its seats are contested every two years.

In 2026, 33 regularly scheduled Senate seats and two special-election seats are on the ballot.

Republicans are defending their congressional majorities, while Democrats hope to gain enough seats to take control.

A change in either chamber would affect the legislation considered, government spending negotiations and congressional oversight of the Trump administration.

Several Senate contests are attracting particular attention. In Georgia, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff faces Republican Mike Collins .

Michigan has an open-seat contest featuring Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers , while New Hampshire's race includes Democrat Chris Pappas and Republican John Sununu .

Other closely watched contests include Maine, where Republican Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson , and North Carolina, where Democrat Roy Cooper and Republican Michael Whatley are competing for an open seat.

Governors and local officials are also on the ballot

Beyond Congress, voters will decide 36 gubernatorial races, alongside contests for state legislatures and other offices. These elections can directly affect policies involving education, taxes, healthcare, housing and public safety.

Depending on where they live, voters may also elect attorneys general, secretaries of state, judges, prosecutors and local representatives. Ballot initiatives could give residents a direct say on proposed laws or amendments to their state's constitution.

The campaigns are being shaped by issues including the cost of living, immigration, healthcare, abortion rights and the economy. The results will determine not only who represents voters in Washington but also who makes important decisions at state and local levels.

How to find your candidates

There is no single ballot for the entire country. The candidates available to each voter depend on their home address and electoral district.

The nonpartisan US Vote Foundation offers election information, while the official USA.gov midterm elections guide helps voters find state-specific guidance. Checking a state's official election website is the best way to confirm polling locations, identification requirements and voting deadlines.

Voters should also review a sample ballot before Election Day so they know which candidates and proposals they will be asked to consider.

The November 3 election could reshape the balance of power in Washington and influence policy across the country. Checking the candidates and races on your own ballot is the first step toward making an informed decision.

articles.title: Theodore Roosevelt, U.S. President: "Whenever you are asked if you can do a job, tell 'em, 'Certainly I can!' Then get busy and find out how to do it"
articles.standfirst: The 26th president of the United States left behind a powerful message about confidence, initiative and learning through action
articles.summary: The 26th president of the United States left behind a powerful message about confidence, initiative and learning through action
articles.body:
T heodore Roosevelt is remembered as one of the most energetic and influential presidents in American history, a leader whose career reflected his belief in taking on challenges rather than standing aside.

One widely shared saying associated with him captures that philosophy in a few words: "Whenever you are asked if you can do a job, tell 'em, 'Certainly I can!' Then get busy and find out how to do it".

The quote offers a practical lesson for anyone facing a new responsibility, whether in the workplace, education or everyday life.

Instead of allowing uncertainty to become an immediate reason to refuse an opportunity, it encourages people to approach the challenge with confidence and then put in the work needed to succeed.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Wednesday, October 28 drawing for the $716 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $716 million
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $716 million
articles.body:
Lottery players are hoping to land a life-changing prize as Powerball prepares for its Wednesday, October 28, 2026 drawing. The jackpot has reached an estimated $716 million after another drawing ended without a ticket matching all six numbers.

The winning numbers for October 28 have not yet been announced. The draw is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, and players should check the official Powerball website after the results are released to confirm the numbers and prize information.

The jackpot has continued to grow since the previous top prize was claimed in August. Monday's drawing, held on October 26, did not produce a jackpot winner, meaning the potential reward has increased for the latest opportunity.

The advertised $716 million figure represents the estimated annuity prize, paid through a series of annual instalments. Winners who prefer to receive their money in a single payment can instead select the estimated cash option of $307.2 million, before taxes.

Previous Powerball results and what players need to know

The most recent completed drawing took place on Monday, October 26. Its winning numbers were 18, 26, 49, 50 and 54, with Powerball 1. The Power Play multiplier was 3x.

Although nobody secured the jackpot, two tickets sold in Florida and Georgia matched all five white balls, earning $1 million each. Those prizes demonstrate that substantial winnings remain possible even without matching the red Powerball number.

Wednesday's draw gives players another opportunity to match the five white balls and the separate red Powerball . The numbers are selected independently, and previous results do not make particular numbers more likely to appear in a future drawing.

The jackpot's size has attracted additional attention, but the odds of winning the top prize remain extremely long.

According to Powerball , the odds of matching all five white balls and the Powerball are approximately 1 in 292.2 million. The overall odds of winning any prize are considerably better, at approximately 1 in 24.9.

How much could the winner actually receive?

The headline jackpot is not necessarily the amount a winner would take home. The annuity option distributes the prize over 30 payments: one initial payment followed by 29 annual payments that increase over time. The cash option provides a smaller amount upfront instead.

Taxes also affect the final payout. Federal withholding applies to large lottery prizes, and the winner's final federal tax liability may be higher than the amount initially withheld. State and local taxes can reduce the prize further, depending on where the winning ticket was purchased and the winner's circumstances.

For that reason, the $716 million figure should be understood as the advertised annuity value rather than a guaranteed lump-sum payment.

Where to check Wednesday's winning numbers

Players can visit the official Powerball website to find the winning numbers once the drawing has concluded. The website also provides previous results, prize details and information about the next scheduled drawing.

Powerball drawings normally take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Ticket-sale deadlines vary by state and jurisdiction, so players should check their local lottery's rules for cutoff times and prize-claim procedures.

Anyone checking a ticket should compare all five white-ball numbers and the red Powerball against the official results, while also checking the Power Play selection if they purchased that option. Tickets should be retained until the result has been verified and any applicable claim instructions reviewed.

With $716 million at stake, Wednesday's drawing is attracting considerable interest. However, until the draw takes place and the official results are published, the October 28 winning numbers remain unknown.

This article will be updated once the confirmed numbers and prize breakdown become available.

articles.summary: Two overlapping promotions are bringing new savings to Costco members, but some offers expire before Thanksgiving
articles.body:
The holiday shopping season is arriving early at Costco , where a new collection of discounts is giving members the chance to stock up on everyday essentials before Thanksgiving and the busy Christmas period.

Rather than relying on a single Black Friday sale, the warehouse retailer is running overlapping promotions throughout November, creating different opportunities to save depending on when customers shop.

Its latest members-only coupon book began on October 19 and runs until November 15, featuring reductions on cleaning supplies, toiletries, food and baking ingredients.

Meanwhile, Costco 's separate Holiday Savings event begins October 30 and continues through November 30, although individual offers may be available for shorter periods.

That distinction matters because customers waiting until Black Friday itself could miss discounts included in the regular November promotion.

Some of the most practical offers involve products that households regularly purchase, particularly those looking to prepare for holiday guests.

Costco is offering $4.50 off 16-packs of Dove Moisturizing Beauty Bars, while Listerine UltraClean Cool Mint Mouthwash is reduced by $4 for a package containing two 1.5-liter bottles.

Laundry supplies are also included, with $6 off Tide + Ultra Oxi Powder Detergent, sold in a 225-ounce container designed to provide approximately 143 loads.

In the kitchen, customers can save $7 on Reynolds Wrap Everyday Aluminum Foil, which comes with two 250-square-foot rolls.

Another potentially useful holiday purchase is Kirkland Signature Alkaline Batteries, with $2 off 48-count packs of AA or AAA batteries.

These offers are available under Costco 's October 19 to November 15 savings period, subject to availability and applicable purchasing conditions.

Holiday groceries and baking essentials

The promotion also offers useful savings for anyone planning Thanksgiving meals or preparing for Christmas entertaining.

Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Bourbon Pure Vanilla Extract is among the larger reductions, with $15 off a package containing two eight-ounce bottles.

Shoppers can also save $3.30 on an 18-stack box of Nabisco Ritz Crackers and $2.70 on a three-pack of Boursin Gourmet Cheese.

The cheese selection includes two Garlic & Fine Herbs varieties and one Shallot & Chive, making it a convenient addition to holiday appetizers.

Pet owners can also take advantage of $5 off a two-pound package of Bocce's Bakery Duck & Blueberry dog treats.

These reductions provide opportunities to buy products ahead of seasonal demand without waiting for Black Friday itself.

When Costco Black Friday 2026 deals start and end

The separate Holiday Savings event begins October 30 and runs through November 30, with different products discounted at different stages of the promotion.

Costco 's advertised offers include savings on selected electronics, home appliances and jewelry, alongside seasonal grocery products. The retailer is also promoting discounts on laptops, televisions and refrigerators.

Members should review individual promotional dates because an item advertised as part of Holiday Savings may not remain discounted throughout November.

Costco will also close its US warehouses on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, making it important to plan shopping trips accordingly.

Customers can check availability and prices through Costco's website or mobile app, although warehouse and online pricing may differ.

The retailer's members-only savings generally require no additional coupon codes, with eligible discounts reflected in the advertised prices.

With two overlapping sales running through November, the best approach is to identify which products are needed and check when their respective discounts expire.

Shoppers seeking everyday household savings have until November 15 to use the current coupon book, while those looking for larger holiday purchases will have additional opportunities throughout the Black Friday promotion.

articles.title: A possible new dwarf planet appears beyond Pluto: what is known about 2026 ED138
articles.standfirst: Astronomers found a dwarf planet on the outskirts of the solar system, beyond Pluto, thanks to the newly inaugurated Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile.
articles.summary: Astronomers found a dwarf planet on the outskirts of the solar system, beyond Pluto, thanks to the newly inaugurated Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile.
articles.body:
The Solar System could have a new member on its official list of dwarf planets. Scientists identified a large icy object orbiting beyond Pluto that, based on its preliminary characteristics, could become one of the largest bodies in this category known so far.

The object, provisionally designated 2026 ED138, was detected thanks to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, located on Cerro Pachón, Chile. Initial calculations place its diameter at between approximately 600 and 1,500 kilometers, although astronomers still need to determine its size more precisely before officially establishing its nature.

2026 ED138 is even farther from the Sun than Pluto

According to the researchers, the new planet, is currently located at a distance from the Sun equivalent to about 46 times the separation between the Earth and our star. By comparison, Pluto orbits at an average distance close to 40 times the one separating the Earth from the Sun.

The discovery was made possible thanks to Rubin's ability to continuously observe large expanses of the sky . The object was located in an area near the plane of the Milky Way, filled with millions of stars, a circumstance that would previously have made its detection difficult. The observatory's systems were able to identify its movement against that enormous stellar background.

Matt Holman, an astrophysicist at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and the one who identified the object, stated that the discovery shows that there are still numerous bodies yet to be found in the most distant regions of the Solar System. The next step will be to establish the physical size of ED138 with greater precision.

The main thing we need to do is establish the physical size of 2026 ED138

What is missing for it to be considered a dwarf planet?

To officially receive that classification, a body must have enough mass for its own gravity to give it an approximately spherical shape.

Available data indicate that 2026 ED138 could meet that condition, but scientists still do not have the measurements needed to confirm it.

One of the problems is that Rubin mainly observes sunlight reflected by the object.

A small but highly reflective body can appear as bright as a larger one with a darker surface. That is why researchers hope to turn to observations at other wavelengths, including the possibility of using ALMA, also located in Chile, to better understand its dimensions.

If it is ultimately classified as a dwarf planet, 2026 ED138 would join the five currently recognized by the International Astronomical Union: Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris. Pluto was part of the list of planets in the Solar System for decades until it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

The discovery also reinforces expectations surrounding the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which began revealing thousands of new Solar System objects during 2026.

In April alone, the observatory reported data corresponding to more than 11,000 new asteroids, a sample of the potential of its observations to discover bodies that had until now gone unnoticed.

articles.title: What time will sunset be after this weekend's Daylight Savings ending for 2026 and everything you need to know about it?
articles.standfirst: Millions of Americans will notice darkness arriving much earlier this weekend as clocks move back one hour
articles.summary: Millions of Americans will notice darkness arriving much earlier this weekend as clocks move back one hour
articles.body:
The sun will disappear below the horizon noticeably earlier across much of the United States this weekend, with the end of daylight saving time bringing an abrupt change to evening routines.

On Sunday, November 1, 2026, Americans in most states will turn their clocks back one hour, shifting the country from daylight saving time to standard time.

Although the adjustment provides an additional hour overnight, it also means sunset will occur approximately 60 minutes earlier according to the clock.

The difference will be especially noticeable in northern cities, where shorter autumn days are already reducing the amount of natural light available after work and school.

New York, Chicago, Boston and Seattle will all experience sunsets before 5 p.m. on Sunday, while southern cities such as Miami and Houston will retain more evening daylight.

What time will sunset be on November 1, 2026?

The precise time depends on geographic location, with northern areas generally experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.

Here are the approximate local sunset times for major US cities on Sunday, November 1.

The change will be particularly striking in northern Maine, where sunset in Caribou is expected at approximately 4:16 p.m.

In contrast, southern locations will continue enjoying daylight later into the afternoon, although they will still experience the one-hour clock adjustment.

When do clocks go back in the United States?

Daylight saving time officially ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, November 1, when clocks move backward to 1 a.m.

That means the hour between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. occurs twice, giving most Americans an additional hour overnight.

Smartphones, computers and other connected devices generally update automatically, while traditional clocks and certain household appliances may require manual changes.

Not every state participates, however. Hawaii and most of Arizona remain on standard time throughout the year, with the Navajo Nation observing daylight saving time as an exception.

Why will it get darker even earlier throughout November?

The clock change doesn't alter the actual amount of daylight, but the Northern Hemisphere will continue experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.

Daylight hours have gradually decreased since the summer solstice in June, with the trend continuing until the winter solstice on December 21.

Seattle, for example, is expected to lose more than 70 minutes of daylight between the beginning and end of November.

The decrease will be less substantial in southern states, where changes in daylight duration are smaller throughout the year.

Despite the earlier sunsets, Americans can expect brighter mornings immediately after the clock change.
